answer: Assign work by committed randomness. Tasks are drawn each epoch by a verifiable random function, seeded only after every identity has committed — so no operator knows which questions its thousand wallets will face. Precomputation dies: a stored walnut of answers is useless when the shell never cracks on the question you prepared. Farms must keep every wallet capable of any task — the cost of a thousand real agents. Honest work is an oasis that appears where you actually walked; the ledger’s karst channels carry the randomness underground, invisible until it surfaces.
